questions.q: Fill up: Vaginal flora is described as ____.
questions.exp: Page 178 opens with 'Vaginal flora: Polymicrobial'.

questions.q: The predominant organism of the vagina is:
questions.exp: 'Lactobacilli / Doderlein bacilli (Predominant)'.

questions.q: Doderlein bacilli are described as:
questions.exp: '- Gram +ve bacilli'.

questions.q: When do lactobacilli first appear?
questions.exp: '- Appears at puberty'.

questions.q: Fill up: Lactobacilli disappear at ____.
questions.exp: '- Disappears at menopause'.

questions.q: The substrate converted to lactic acid is:
questions.exp: 'Glycogen in stratified epithelium → Lactic acid + H2O2'.

questions.q: Fill up: Glycogen breakdown yields lactic acid and ____.
questions.exp: The arrow prints 'Lactic acid + H2O2'.

questions.q: The acidic pH produced by lactobacilli is described as the:
questions.exp: '→ Acidic pH → Defense mechanism'.

questions.q: Which hormone is responsible for the presence of glycogen?
questions.exp: '- Estrogen: Responsible for presence of glycogen'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ survives in the acidic pH produced by lactobacilli.
questions.exp: '- Candida: Survives in acidic pH'.

questions.q: Which two findings are printed under 'normal pap smear'?
questions.exp: The pap smear block lists 'Doderlein bacilli' and 'Superficial cells' under 'Normal pap smear'.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the pap smear here?
questions.exp: 'Pap smear: Screening for cancer'.

questions.q: Scenario: A postmenopausal woman has recurrent vaginal infections. Which printed fact explains the loss of her defence mechanism?
opts: Lactobacilli disappear at menopause, so the acidic protective pH is lost
questions.exp: The printed line 'Disappears at menopause' explains the loss of lactobacilli and acidic protection.

questions.q: True/False: Oestrogen protects the vagina by causing glycogen deposition that lactobacilli convert to lactic acid.
opts: False - progesterone is responsible for glycogen
False - glycogen is dietary in origin
questions.exp: The chain printed is estrogen → glycogen → lactic acid → acidic pH → defence.

questions.q: Odd one out - which organism is NOT described as part of the normal protective flora?
questions.exp: Gardnerella is the bacterial vaginosis organism, not normal protective flora.

questions.q: Fill up: Leucorrhoea is described as ____ white discharge.
questions.exp: 'Leucorrhoea: Physiological white discharge'.

questions.q: When is physiological discharge increased?
opts: In the early follicular phase only
questions.exp: 'Increased: During ovulation, Before menstruation'.

questions.q: Fill up: In the first half of the cycle the discharge is thin and watery because of ____.
questions.exp: '- 1st half of cycle: Thin watery d/t estrogen'.

questions.q: In the second half of the cycle the discharge becomes thick because of:
questions.exp: '- 2nd half of cycle: Thick d/t progesterone'.

questions.q: Which three characteristics define physiological leucorrhoea?
opts: Colourless, odourless and without pruritus or dysuria
questions.exp: The characteristics block lists colourless, odourless and 'No pruritis/dysuria'.

questions.q: Fill up: The differential listed against leucorrhoea is ____ vaginosis discharge.
questions.exp: 'D/d: Bacterial vaginosis discharge'.

questions.q: How does bacterial vaginosis discharge differ from physiological leucorrhoea in the printed comparison?
opts: It is curdy white with excoriation
It is colourless but has a pungent fishy odour and no pruritus
questions.exp: BV discharge is printed as colourless with a pungent/fishy odour and no pruritus.

questions.q: Match the discharge feature with the diagnosis - 1) Thin watery in the first half of cycle 2) Thick in the second half 3) Pungent fishy odour, colourless 4) Curdy white ... A) Bacterial vaginosis B) Physiological leucorrhoea C) Candidiasis
questions.exp: Cycle-related changes are physiological; fishy colourless discharge is BV; curdy white is candidiasis.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman reports increased clear discharge mid-cycle with no smell and no itching. What is the printed interpretation?
opts: Physiological leucorrhoea of the ovulatory phase
questions.exp: Mid-cycle thin watery discharge without odour or pruritus is physiological.

questions.q: True/False: Physiological leucorrhoea is associated with pruritus and dysuria.
opts: True - pruritus is the main complaint
questions.exp: The printed characteristics explicitly state no pruritus and no dysuria.

questions.q: Fill up: The organism named for bacterial vaginosis is ____ vaginalis.
questions.exp: 'Gardnerella vaginalis' heads the BV organism list.

questions.q: Which two additional organisms are listed with Gardnerella in bacterial vaginosis?
questions.exp: The BV organism list is Gardnerella vaginalis, mycoplasma and mobiluncus.

questions.q: Fill up: The candida species named is Candida ____.
questions.exp: 'Candida albicans'.

questions.q: Trichomonas vaginalis is described as a:
questions.exp: 'Trichomonas vaginalis: Flagellated protozoan'.

questions.q: Fill up: Bacterial vaginosis is described as an alteration of vaginal ____.
questions.exp: 'Alteration of vaginal flora'.

questions.q: Which vaginitis is printed as the most common vaginitis in females?
questions.exp: 'm/c vaginitis in female' is printed in the BV column.

questions.q: Which vaginitis is the most common in pregnant females?
questions.exp: '- m/c vaginitis in pregnant female' appears in the candida column.

questions.q: Which three predisposing factors are listed for candidiasis?
questions.exp: The predisposing list is pregnancy, immunocompromised, antibiotics/steroids/OCP consumption.

questions.q: Fill up: Trichomonas is associated with alteration of vaginal pH towards the ____ range.
questions.exp: 'Alteration of vaginal pH (Alkaline)'.

questions.q: Trichomonas vaginitis is noted to coexist with:
questions.exp: 'Coexist with bacterial vaginosis'.

questions.q: Which discharge colour is printed for trichomonas?
questions.exp: 'Frothy / Yellowish green colour'.

questions.q: Fill up: The candida discharge is curdy white, like ____ cheese.
questions.exp: 'Curdy white / cottage cheese'.

questions.q: Which pH is printed for candida?
questions.exp: The candida column prints pH < 4.5.

questions.q: Which two of the three vaginitides have a pH of 4.5 or above?
questions.exp: BV and trichomonas print pH >= 4.5; only candida is below.

questions.q: Fill up: Bacterial vaginosis is marked with a cross against pruritus, meaning ____ inflammation.
questions.exp: '× (No inflammation)' is printed for BV.

questions.q: In which vaginitis is excoriation the main complaint?
questions.exp: The candida column prints 'Intense pruritis → Excoriation: main complaint'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ dysuria is listed under trichomonas vaginitis.
questions.exp: 'Splash dysuria'.

questions.q: The polymorphonuclear leucocyte to epithelial cell ratio printed for bacterial vaginosis is:
questions.exp: 'PMNs / epithelial cells: <1'.

questions.q: Which vaginitis is marked as a sexually transmitted disease in the table?
questions.exp: The STD row is marked against trichomonas.

questions.q: Match each finding with the vaginitis - 1) Clue cells 2) Cottage-cheese discharge 3) Strawberry cervix 4) pH below 4.5 ... A) Trichomonas B) Bacterial vaginosis C) Candidiasis
questions.exp: Clue cells are BV; cottage cheese and low pH are candida; strawberry cervix is trichomonas.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has profuse frothy yellow-green discharge, an itchy vulva and pain on passing urine. Which vaginitis?
questions.exp: Frothy yellowish green discharge with pruritus and splash dysuria is trichomonas.

questions.q: True/False: Bacterial vaginosis shows abundant polymorphonuclear leucocytes on microscopy.
opts: True - it is an inflammatory condition
questions.exp: BV is marked 'No inflammation' with a PMN/epithelial ratio below 1.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed predisposing factor for candidiasis?
questions.exp: Alkaline pH is the trichomonas column, not a candida predisposing factor.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for vaginitis is ____ microscopy.
questions.exp: 'IOC: Saline microscopy'.

questions.q: A clue cell is defined as:
opts: A yeast cell with a bud
An epithelial cell with bacteria adhered to it
A flagellated organism the size of a nucleus
questions.exp: 'Epithelial cells with bacteria adhered: Clue cell'.

questions.q: Which gram-stain scoring system is named for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.exp: '- Nugent score: Score 7-10'.

questions.q: Fill up: The two candida forms seen on microscopy are pseudohyphae and ____.
questions.exp: 'Pseudohyphae' and 'Spores of candida'.

questions.q: Which microscopy appearance is printed for candida spores?
questions.exp: 'Tennis racket appearance'.

questions.q: On saline microscopy, trichomonas is identified by:
opts: Motility, or a pear-shaped organism the size of a cell nucleus
questions.exp: 'motility + (or) Pear shaped organism = Size of nucleus of cells'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gold standard test for candidiasis is culture on ____ media.
questions.exp: 'Culture on Sabouraud media' is placed beside 'Gold standard test'.

questions.q: Which per-speculum findings are printed for trichomonas?
opts: Strawberry cervix and angry looking vagina
questions.exp: 'p/s examination: Strawberry cervix / Angry looking vagina'.

questions.q: Fill up: The named test for bacterial vaginosis is the ____ test.
questions.exp: 'Named test' points to the whiff test.

questions.q: What is added to the discharge in the whiff test and what odour results?
opts: Acetic acid, producing a yeasty odour
Lugol iodine, producing a metallic odour
Ten percent KOH, producing a fishy amine-like odour
questions.exp: 'Add 10% KOH to discharge → fishy / amine like odour'.

questions.q: How many Amsel criteria are listed?
questions.exp: Greyish white discharge, pH >= 4.5, clue cells >= 20%, whiff test positive.

questions.q: How many Amsel criteria must be positive to diagnose bacterial vaginosis?
questions.exp: '3/4 positive → Diagnostic'.

questions.q: Fill up: Amsel criterion 3 requires clue cells in at least ____ percent of epithelial cells.
questions.exp: 'Clue cells >= 20% of epithelial cells'.

questions.q: Which Amsel criterion sets the pH threshold?
questions.exp: Criterion 2 is 'pH >= 4.5'.

questions.q: Match each Amsel criterion with its position - 1) Greyish white discharge 2) pH >= 4.5 3) Clue cells >= 20% 4) Whiff test positive ... A) 4 B) 2 C) 1 D) 3
questions.exp: The printed order is discharge, pH, clue cells, whiff test.

questions.q: Which of the three vaginitides has a negative whiff test?
questions.exp: The candida column prints 'whiff test -ve'; BV and trichomonas are positive.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has a greyish white discharge, vaginal pH 5.2 and clue cells in 30% of epithelial cells, but a negative whiff test. Does she meet Amsel criteria?
opts: Yes - three of four criteria are met
No - the whiff test is mandatory
questions.exp: Discharge, pH and clue cells give three positive criteria out of four.

questions.q: True/False: The whiff test uses ten percent potassium hydroxide and is positive in both bacterial vaginosis and trichomonas.
opts: False - it is positive only in BV
False - it is negative in both
questions.exp: BV and trichomonas columns both print whiff test positive, and KOH 10% is the reagent.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed microscopy finding for vaginitis?
questions.exp: Intracellular diplococci belong to the gonorrhoea section, not the vaginitis microscopy row.

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice for bacterial vaginosis in the non-pregnant woman is oral ____ 500 mg twice daily for 7 days.
questions.exp: 'metronidazole: Oral 500 mg BD x 7 days'.

questions.q: Which alternative single-dose regimen is printed for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.exp: The bracket reads '(or) 2 gram stat'.

questions.q: Which second drug is listed for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.exp: 'Clindamycin' is the alternative named.

questions.q: Fill up: The treatment of candidiasis is oral fluconazole ____ mg stat.
questions.exp: 'Oral fluconazole: 150 mg stat'.

questions.q: What is the non-pregnant regimen for trichomonas vaginitis?
opts: Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days, or 2 g stat
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
questions.exp: The trichomonas column prints metronidazole 500 mg BD x 7 days or 2 g stat.

questions.q: In the first trimester, how should metronidazole be given?
questions.exp: '- 1st trimester: Vaginal metronidazole'.

questions.q: Fill up: From the second trimester onwards, metronidazole is given ____.
questions.exp: '- 2nd/3rd trimester: Oral metronidazole'.

questions.q: Which drug is contraindicated in pregnancy for candidiasis?
opts: Oral metronidazole in the third trimester
questions.exp: 'Oral fluconazole: Contraindicated'.

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice for candidiasis in pregnancy is topical ____.
questions.exp: 'Topical clotrimazole: DOC'.

questions.q: Partner treatment in bacterial vaginosis is advised:
questions.exp: 'Partner Rx: For symptomatic partners only'.

questions.q: Is partner treatment indicated in candidiasis?
questions.exp: The candida column marks partner treatment with a cross.

questions.q: Fill up: For trichomonas, the partner receives metronidazole at the ____ dose.
questions.exp: '- Dose: Same'.

questions.q: Match each vaginitis with its pregnancy modification - 1) BV in the first trimester 2) BV after the first trimester 3) Candidiasis in pregnancy 4) Trichomonas in the first trimester ... A) Oral metronidazole B) Vaginal metronidazole C) Topical clotrimazole
questions.exp: Metronidazole is vaginal in the first trimester and oral later; candida needs topical clotrimazole.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman at 8 weeks of gestation has bacterial vaginosis. What is the printed route of metronidazole?
questions.exp: First trimester metronidazole is given vaginally.

questions.q: True/False: Oral fluconazole can be used safely in the first trimester for candidiasis.
opts: True - after the first trimester only
questions.exp: Oral fluconazole is printed as contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which drug is NOT part of the printed vaginitis treatment set?
questions.exp: Cefixime belongs to the cervicitis and PID kits, not vaginitis treatment.

questions.q: Fill up: The ectocervix is lined by stratified ____ epithelium, like the vagina.
questions.exp: 'Ectocervix: Stratified squamous epithelium (Like vagina)'.

questions.q: The endocervix is lined by:
questions.exp: 'Endocervix: Lined by Columnar epithelium'.

questions.q: Which four infections may involve the ectocervix?
questions.exp: The ectocervix list is candida, trichomonas, HSV and HPV.

questions.q: Which two organisms infect the endocervix?
questions.exp: The endocervix list is chlamydia and gonorrhoea, with 'Infection of endocervix → Cervicitis'.

questions.q: Fill up: Infection of the ____ is what the page defines as cervicitis.
questions.exp: The bracket reads '(Infection of endocervix → Cervicitis)'.

questions.q: Match the epithelium with the infections listed - 1) Ectocervix 2) Endocervix ... A) Chlamydia and gonorrhoea B) Candida, trichomonas, HSV and HPV
questions.exp: Squamous ectocervix hosts the vaginal infections; columnar endocervix hosts chlamydia and gonorrhoea.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has a cervical swab growing Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Which part of the cervix is infected?
questions.exp: Gonorrhoea is listed as an endocervical infection producing cervicitis.

questions.q: True/False: HPV infection of the cervix is listed under endocervical infections.
questions.exp: HPV is listed with the ectocervical (vaginal-type) infections.

questions.q: Odd one out - which infection is NOT listed under the ectocervix?
questions.exp: Gonorrhoea is an endocervical infection.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common route of spread is ascending infection along with ____.
questions.exp: 'm/c route of spread: Ascending infection along with sperms (STD)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common site of infection is the endocervix rather than the ____.
questions.exp: 'm/c site: Endocervix > Urethra'.

questions.q: What proportion of cases are asymptomatic?
questions.exp: 'Asymptomatic (50-80%)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common presentation is a ____ discharge.
questions.exp: 'Discharge (m/c presentation): mucoid/purulent'.

questions.q: Which two additional symptoms are listed?
questions.exp: 'Dyspareunia' and 'Post coital bleeding'.

questions.q: Match each item with its status - 1) Asymptomatic 2) Discharge 3) Dyspareunia 4) Post-coital bleeding ... A) Most common presentation B) 50-80% C) Listed symptom D) Listed symptom
questions.exp: Asymptomatic in 50-80%; discharge is the commonest presentation; dyspareunia and post-coital bleeding are additional.

questions.q: Scenario: A 24-year-old has a mucopurulent cervical discharge and bleeding after intercourse but no pain. What is the most likely finding on testing?
questions.exp: Mucopurulent discharge with post-coital bleeding in a young woman is the printed cervicitis picture.

questions.q: True/False: The majority of women with chlamydial cervicitis are symptomatic.
questions.exp: 50-80% are asymptomatic.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed presentation of cervicitis?
questions.exp: Cyclical pain belongs to the cryptomenorrhoea page.

questions.q: Which three per-speculum findings are printed?
opts: Unhealthy friable cervix, bleeding on touch, and erosion or ulcer
questions.exp: Per speculum: unhealthy friable cervix, bleeds on touch, erosion/ulcer.

questions.q: Fill up: The differential to be excluded when these findings are present is ____.
questions.exp: 'D/d: PID' with uterine and adnexal tenderness.

questions.q: Which two findings on per-vaginal examination would shift the diagnosis to PID?
opts: Cervical motion tenderness and vaginal discharge
questions.exp: The D/d block lists uterine tenderness and adnexal tenderness.

questions.q: In uncomplicated cervicitis, the uterus on per-vaginal examination is:
questions.exp: 'Uterus: Normal'.

questions.q: Fill up: In uncomplicated cervicitis the adnexa are ____.
questions.exp: 'Adnexa: Normal'.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with a friable cervix that bleeds on touch also has adnexal tenderness. What does the printed page suggest?
opts: Consider pelvic inflammatory disease rather than isolated cervicitis
questions.exp: Adnexal tenderness is the D/d pointer to PID.

questions.q: True/False: Cervical motion tenderness is listed as a per-speculum finding.
opts: True - it is the first per-speculum finding
questions.exp: Cervical motion tenderness belongs to the PID criteria; per-speculum findings are appearance-based.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed per-speculum finding in cervicitis?
questions.exp: Adnexal tenderness is a per-vaginal finding pointing to PID.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonorrhoea is described as Gram ____ diplococci.
questions.exp: 'Gram -ve diplococci'.

questions.q: Gonococcal diplococci are described as:
questions.exp: 'Intra/extracellular'.

questions.q: Fill up: On Gram stain, the criterion printed is more than ____ neutrophils per field.
questions.exp: '>10 Neutrophils/field'.

questions.q: Which organism shows no organism on Gram stain?
questions.exp: The chlamydia column prints 'No organism'.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for both organisms is the nucleic acid ____ test.
questions.exp: 'IOC: Nucleic acid amplification test'.

questions.q: Which specimen is advised for gonorrhoea when urethritis is present?
opts: Urine, in addition to the endocervical swab
questions.exp: 'Specimen: Endocervical swab; Urine if urethritis +ve'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gold standard for gonorrhoea is culture on ____ media.
questions.exp: 'Gold standard: Culture on Thayer Martin media'.

questions.q: The gold standard for chlamydia is culture on:
questions.exp: 'Gold standard: Culture on McCoy cell lines'.

questions.q: Match each organism with its gold standard - 1) Gonorrhoea 2) Chlamydia ... A) Culture on McCoy cell lines B) Culture on Thayer Martin media
questions.exp: Thayer Martin for gonorrhoea; McCoy cell lines for chlamydia.

questions.q: Scenario: A cervical Gram stain shows more than 10 neutrophils per field but no organism. Which diagnosis is favoured?
questions.exp: Polymorphs without a visible organism is the chlamydia pattern.

questions.q: True/False: NAAT is listed as the gold standard for chlamydia.
questions.exp: NAAT is the investigation of choice; culture on McCoy cell lines is the gold standard.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed specimen or test for cervicitis?
questions.exp: Sabouraud media is the candidiasis gold standard.

questions.q: Fill up: In the non-pregnant patient, chlamydia is treated with doxycycline 100 mg ____ for 7 days.
questions.exp: Printed: 'Tab. Doxycycline 100mg OD x 7 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonorrhoea is treated with Inj. Ceftriaxone ____ mg IM as a single dose.
questions.exp: Printed: 'Inj Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose'.

questions.q: Which drug is contraindicated in pregnancy in this treatment block?
questions.exp: 'Doxycycline: C/I' under the pregnant row.

questions.q: Fill up: The pregnant patient is treated with tablet azithromycin ____ g orally as a single dose.
questions.exp: 'Tab. Azithromycin 1 g oral: Single dose'.

questions.q: Which two complications of cervicitis are printed?
opts: PID from ascending infection, and perihepatitis (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome)
questions.exp: 'Complications: PID (d/t ascend of infection), Perihepatitis: Fitz Hugh Curtis syndrome'.

questions.q: Fill up: The perihepatitis of this infection is called Fitz-Hugh-____ syndrome.
questions.exp: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is the named perihepatitis.

questions.q: Match each drug with its setting - 1) Doxycycline 100 mg OD x 7 days 2) Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose 3) Azithromycin 1 g single dose 4) Doxycycline in pregnancy ... A) Contraindicated B) Pregnant patient C) Gonorrhoea, non-pregnant D) Chlamydia, non-pregnant
questions.exp: Doxycycline for non-pregnant chlamydia, ceftriaxone for gonorrhoea, azithromycin in pregnancy, doxycycline contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.q: Scenario: A pregnant woman with cervicitis cannot receive doxycycline. What is the printed alternative?
opts: Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose
questions.exp: Azithromycin 1 g single dose is the pregnant patient's regimen.

questions.q: True/False: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is listed as a complication of vaginitis.
questions.exp: It is a complication of cervicitis from ascending infection.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT in the printed cervicitis treatment block?
questions.exp: Metronidazole 400 mg BD for 14 days belongs to the PID regimen.

questions.q: Fill up: Syndromic management is advised by ____.
questions.exp: 'Syndromic management: Advised by NACO'.

questions.q: Colour-coded kits are based on which four inputs?
opts: History, per-speculum examination, per-vaginal examination and minimal investigation
Examination, pH, whiff test and microscopy
History, partner history, pap smear and culture
questions.exp: 'Colour coded kits: Based on History + P/s examination + P/v examination + minimal investigation'.

questions.q: Fill up: The vaginitis kit is the ____ kit.
questions.exp: Green kit is the vaginitis kit.

questions.q: What is in the green kit?
opts: Secnidazole 2 g plus fluconazole 150 mg stat
questions.exp: 'Green Kit 2: Secnidazole 2 gms + Fluconazole 150 mg stat'.

questions.q: Fill up: The cervicitis kit is the ____ kit, number 1.
questions.exp: 'Grey Kit 1' is the cervicitis kit.

questions.q: What two drugs are in the grey kit?
opts: Azithromycin 1 g stat and cefixime 400 mg stat
questions.exp: 'Grey Kit 1: Tab Azithromycin 1 gm OD stat + Tab Cefixime 400mg OD stat'.

questions.q: Fill up: The PID kit is the ____ kit, number 6.
questions.exp: 'Yellow Kit 6' is the PID kit.

questions.q: Which three drugs make up the yellow kit?
opts: Azithromycin 1 g, cefixime 400 mg and secnidazole 2 g
Ceftriaxone 250 mg, doxycycline 100 mg and metronidazole 400 mg
Fluconazole 150 mg, secnidazole 2 g and clotrimazole
Cefixime 400 mg stat, metronidazole 400 mg BD for 14 days and doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days
questions.exp: The printed yellow kit contains those three drugs.

questions.q: Which extra step is mandated before using the yellow kit?
questions.exp: 'R/o: Ectopic pregnancy' is printed in the PID row.

questions.q: Fill up: The partner of a PID patient receives grey kit number ____.
questions.exp: The partner treatment for PID is 'No. 1: Grey kit'.

questions.q: Which clinical findings route a patient to the yellow kit?
opts: Lower abdominal pain with any one of uterine, cervical movement or adnexal tenderness
Vaginal discharge with a healthy cervix
Post-coital bleeding with a normal cervix
questions.exp: The yellow kit row requires lower abdominal pain plus any one tenderness finding.

questions.q: Supportive advice common to the kits includes abstinence for how many days?
questions.exp: 'Supportive treatment: Abstinence x 7 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: Partner treatment is indicated in cervicitis and PID but ____ in vaginitis.
questions.exp: 'Partner Rx: Cervicitis & PID - Not indicated in vaginitis'.

questions.q: Which three other conditions are listed as uses of kit 1?
opts: Vaginal discharge, pelvic pain and dysuria
Cervical erosion, post-coital bleeding and infertility
Anorectal discharge, scrotal pain syndrome and urethritis
questions.exp: 'Other uses of Kit 1: Anorectal discharge, Scrotal pain syndrome, Urethritis'.

questions.q: Match the presentation with the kit - 1) Discharge with pruritus, healthy cervix 2) Unhealthy friable cervix 3) Lower abdominal pain with adnexal tenderness ... A) Yellow kit 6 B) Green kit 2 C) Grey kit 1
questions.exp: Vaginitis takes green, cervicitis grey, PID yellow.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has vaginal discharge and dysuria; the cervix looks healthy and the per-vaginal examination is normal. Which kit?
opts: Grey kit for her and yellow for her partner
questions.exp: Discharge with pruritus/dysuria, a healthy cervix and a normal per-vaginal examination is the vaginitis row.

questions.q: True/False: The yellow kit is used for the partner of a woman with PID.
opts: True - partners receive the same kit
questions.exp: The partner receives grey kit 1 (cefixime and azithromycin).

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a listed use of kit 1?
opts: Vaginal discharge with a healthy cervix
questions.exp: Vaginal discharge with a healthy cervix routes to the green kit.
